sections.heading: Opening
paragraphs: Per the file, a node typically spends its time validating blocks. Per the file, if, however, a staker (per the file) delegates its stake to a node, it will occasionally be (per the file) selected as a _slot leader_. Per the file, as a slot leader, the node is responsible for producing (per the file) blocks during an assigned _slot_. Per the file, a slot has a (per the file) duration of some number of preconfigured _ticks_. Per the file, the duration of those (per the file) ticks are estimated with (per the file) a _PoH Recorder_ described (per the file) later in this document. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: BankFork
paragraphs: Per the file, bankFork tracks changes to (per the file) the bank state over a specific slot. Per the file, once the final tick (per the file) has been registered the state is frozen. Per the file, any attempts to write to are rejected. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Validator
paragraphs: Per the file, a node operates on many different (per the file) concurrent forks of the (per the file) bank state until it (per the file) generates a PoH hash (per the file) with a height within its leader slot. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Slot Leader
paragraphs: Per the file, a slot leader builds (per the file) blocks on top of (per the file) only one fork, the (per the file) one it last voted on. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: PoH Recorder
paragraphs: Per the file, slot leaders and nodes use a PoH Recorder (per the file) for both estimating slot (per the file) height and for recording txs. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: PoH Recorder when Validating
paragraphs: Per the file, the PoH Recorder acts (per the file) as a simple VDF when validating. Per the file, it tells the node when it needs to (per the file) switch to the slot leader role. Per the file, every time the node votes on a fork, (per the file) it should use the (per the file) fork's latest blockhash to re-seed the VDF. Per the file, re-seeding solves two problems. Per the file, first, it synchronizes its (per the file) VDF to the leader's, (per the file) allowing it to more accurately (per the file) determine when its leader slot begins. Per the file, second, if the previous (per the file) leader goes down, all (per the file) wallclock time is accounted (per the file) for in the next (per the file) leader's PoH stream. Per the file, for example, if one (per the file) block is missing when (per the file) the leader starts, the (per the file) block it produces should (per the file) have a PoH duration of two blocks. Per the file, the longer duration ensures (per the file) the following leader isn't (per the file) attempting to snip all the txs from the previous leader's slot. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: PoH Recorder when Leading
paragraphs: Per the file, a slot leader use (per the file) the PoH Recorder to record txs, locking their positions in time. Per the file, the PoH hash has to be derived from a (per the file) previous leader's last block. Per the file, if it isn't, its (per the file) block will fail PoH verification (per the file) and be rejected by the cluster. Per the file, the PoH Recorder also (per the file) serves to inform the (per the file) slot leader when its slot is over. Per the file, the leader needs to (per the file) take care not to (per the file) modify its bank if recording the tx would generate a PoH (per the file) height outside its designated slot. Per the file, the leader, therefore, should not commit acct changes until after it (per the file) generates the entry's PoH hash.

Per the file, when the PoH height (per the file) falls outside its slot any txs in its pipeline may (per the file) be dropped or forwarded (per the file) to the next leader. Per the file, forwarding is preferred, as (per the file) it would minimize network (per the file) congestion, allowing the cluster (per the file) to advertise higher TPS capacity. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Validator Loop
paragraphs: Per the file, the PoH Recorder manages (per the file) the transition between modes. Per the file, once a ledger is replayed, the node can run until the recorder indicates it ought to be the slot leader. Per the file, as a slot leader, (per the file) the node can then execute and record txs. Per the file, the loop is synchronized (per the file) to PoH and does (per the file) a synchronous start and (per the file) stop of the slot leader functionality. Per the file, after stopping, the node's TVU should find itself (per the file) in the same state as (per the file) if a different leader had (per the file) sent it the same block. Per the file, the following is pseudocode for the loop: Query the LeaderScheduler for (per the file) the next assigned slot.

Per the file, run the TVU over all the forks. Per the file, tVU will send votes (per the file) to what it believes (per the file) is the "best" fork. Per the file, after each vote, restart (per the file) the PoH Recorder to (per the file) run until the next assigned slot. Per the file, when time to be (per the file) a slot leader, start the TPU. Per the file, point it to the (per the file) last fork the TVU voted on. Per the file, produce entries until the (per the file) end of the slot. Per the file, for the duration of (per the file) the slot, the TVU (per the file) must not vote on other forks. Per the file, after the slot ends, (per the file) the TPU freezes its BankFork. Per the file, after freezing, the TVU may resume voting.
